facts.what: 叙述者童年时母亲曾整整一个周末不见人影；她因为会开罐头而活了下来；她说童年有些时刻她希望从没发生过（母亲叫不醒、她得敲门求助）。

anchors.anchor: She disappeared once for a whole weekend, but I knew how to use a can opener, so I survived.
times when my mother wasn’t waking up and I was scared and I had to knock on doors to get help

facts.what: 母亲唯一一次对叙述者失望，是因为她退学；叙述者觉得这很讽刺，因为母亲当年若愿意本可以像所有纽约的好犹太女孩一样去 City College；而且叙述者没有立刻把退学的事告诉母亲。

anchors.anchor: I only ever disappointed her once, as far as I know.
She didn’t like that I dropped out of college, which I thought was rich.
She could have gone to City College like all the good Jewish girls of New York if she had wanted to.
I hadn’t told her right away.

facts.what: 母亲当面说「我以为你会跟我不同」；叙述者回「我不知道你还有标准」；叙述者说这番话令她愤怒到多年未有；母亲反驳说她从幼儿时期就自己做选择、每天早上自己穿衣服。

anchors.anchor: I thought you were going to be different from me
I didn’t know you had standards
It incensed me, in a way I haven’t gotten angry for years
You’ve been making your own choices since you were a toddler. You dressed yourself every morning.

facts.what: 母亲那年有一身她称为「ailments」的病痛；叙述者当年没有立刻意识到她病得多重，日后希望自己当时看出来并帮上忙；她把母亲身上发生的事登记为「Ruthie Problems」，从小就学会在情感上尽量与自己的事分开。

anchors.anchor: that’s what she called them, her ailments
I think I registered whatever was going on as Ruthie Problems, which I had learned from a young age to keep separate from my own

facts.what: 母亲最后一套公寓在 Twelfth 街，介于第三与第二大道之间；那栋楼建在马路对面 St. Mark's 的墓地上（她后来才知道）；叙述者至今避开走那条街，说那里像被某种古老、不认可、不轻易宽恕的东西盯着。

anchors.anchor: My mother’s last apartment was on Twelfth between Third and Second.
The building was built over burial grounds for St. Mark’s across the avenue.
I still avoid walking down that block, but not just because of her.

facts.what: 母亲在街上遇到 Franny 时正在走她所谓的「river to rivers」（从东走到西再走回来，是她需要清醒时做的）；Franny 请母亲住进自己的公寓、帮她照看植物；母亲大约一周后就与整栋楼成了好朋友；叙述者推断 Franny 当时心想「这个女人不好」，并说 Franny 在母亲生命的最后一年为她做的比自己多。

anchors.anchor: My mother ran into Franny on the street when she was taking one of her
she asked my mother to stay in her place and take care of her plants
Franny did more for my mother in the last year of her life than I did.
was best friends with the whole building after about a week

facts.what: Ruthie 死后，Mark 和 Bianca 帮叙述者打扫公寓（实情是他们在打扫，叙述者坐在沙发上喝酒、哭、吐在皮沙发上）；她给 Franny 留了一张告知母亲死讯的便条；几个月后 Mark 告诉她留言机上有 Franny 的留言，她把留言删了。

anchors.anchor: they cleaned the apartment while I sat and drank and wept and puked on her couch
I left Franny a note that my mother had died.
there was a message on the machine from her, but I erased it

facts.what: 叙述者原以为母亲从不出现在她面前做鬼魂，是因母亲不想添麻烦、像在帮她一个忙；但既然 Mark 也没为她出现，她不得不认定这里有个共同分母，那就是她自己——在他们最难的日子里她都没到场，所以他们凭什么为她出现。

anchors.anchor: I never saw my mother as a ghost because she didn’t want to be a bother
I had to think there was a common denominator here, and it was me
I hadn’t shown up for them, so why would they show up for me?

relations.note: 叙述者羡慕所有母亲还在且没有把她逐出家门的人；母亲从不出现在她面前做鬼魂，她先是解释为母亲不想添麻烦。

anchors.anchor: I was envious of everyone whose mother was around and didn’t actively disown them.

relations.note: 叙述者说她对 Cynthia 与她母亲的关系了解不多，所以知道自己不该苛评，但她是羡慕的。

anchors.anchor: I didn’t know a lot about Cynthia’s relationship with her mother, so I knew I shouldn’t judge it too harshly, but I was envious.

relations.note: Lupe 认识她女儿、爱她，并且让她过自己的生活（叙述者羡慕的对象之一）。

anchors.anchor: Lupe knew her daughter and loved her and let her live her life.

relations.note: Julie 的母亲完全不知道她的事，但为那些她能理解的部分感到骄傲。

anchors.anchor: Julie’s mother didn’t know about her at all but she was proud of the things she could understand.

relations.note: 叙述者明确说自己 envy 了 Bianca 和 Julie。

anchors.anchor: I envied Bianca and Julie.

relations.note: 对照组：Tanya 的妈总让她去店里买一瓶红酒当午餐；而叙述者的母亲从没那样使唤她，多半只是让她自己照顾自己。

anchors.anchor: Tanya’s mom, who always had her going to the store to get a bottle of red wine for lunch
She mostly just left me to take care of myself.

relations.note: Franny 是母亲的老朋友，另一个从 Bronx 搬到 Village 的「Party daughter」，只是 Franny 混出了头：学艺术史、去巴黎、回来成了很时髦的女同性恋，并拿到去罗马写作的 fellowship，因此请母亲住进她的公寓照看植物。

anchors.anchor: her old friend Franny, another Party daughter who decamped from the Bronx to the Village
studied art history, went to Paris, came back a very chic lesbian
Franny had a fellowship to go write in Rome or something

relations.note: 她躺在 Franny 的床上，哭湿 Franny 的丝绸枕套，希望 Franny 是她母亲，或者她就是 Franny，或者 Franny 和她母亲彼此相爱过，好让母亲人生里有一件事转向。

anchors.anchor: wished Franny was my mother, or that I was Franny, or that Franny and my mother had loved each other

relations.note: Mark 也曾缺席：叙述者把母亲与 Mark 都「没为她出现」并列，作为共同分母是自己的依据。

anchors.anchor: But since Mark, too, hadn’t shown up for me
